key_insight: QAOA serves as a useful benchmark for distributed quantum computing because its graph-based communication patterns expose how topology, routing, and entanglement management shape performance in switch-based quantum networks.
engineering_relevance: For quantum data-center design, the study shows that compiler-aware routing and network topology choices can materially affect latency and entanglement overhead in real distributed workloads.
method: Extended SwitchQNet with a routing generator for QAOA cost terms
Converted two-qubit graph interactions into remote-CX requests across QPUs
Compared Clos, fat-tree, and spine-leaf networks under different buffer, look-ahead, qubit, latency, and fidelity settings
evidence_signal: Across the evaluated topologies and parameter sweeps, QAOA showed modest but consistent latency reductions, alongside measured EPR overhead, wait time, and retry costs.
watch_item: The performance gains are modest and likely sensitive to assumptions about EPR latency, fidelity, buffering, and switch reconfiguration overhead, so results may not generalize without hardware-specific validation.
paper_title: Performance Analysis of QAOA Across Distributed Quantum Network Topologies Using SwitchQNet
